inputs.proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.
inputs.original_proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.

blockers: claim: Hard-coded channel index 0 instead of dynamically determining the correct channel for poll PID requests. The original code used channel_index_for_rx() to find the appropriate channel, but the new code unconditionally uses t->chans[0], which will access an incorrect channel or cause undefined behavior if chan_count is 0.; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: build_mode01_request(req, t->chans[0].tx_id, t->poll_pid);

claim: The backstop check for poll mode channels was removed. The original code checked (sched_mode || params.poll_pid != 0) && t->chan_count == 0, catching both scheduler and poll cases. The new code only checks sched_mode && t->chan_count == 0, allowing poll mode to proceed without any channel validation.; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: if (sched_mode && t->chan_count == 0) {
questions: What is the relationship between rx_id and the filter parameter? The parse_query check for 'poll without filter' uses p->rx_id == 0, but the comment refers to the filter parameter. Does rx_id get populated from filter or from profile channels?
Is the struct j2534_uri_params definition available? I need to verify what fields are in this struct to confirm whether rx_id is the correct field to check for poll without filter.
nits: The comment change in j2534_transport.cpp struct definition for poll_pid field references 'raw-profile debug override' but this should be clarified - is this still accurate given the scheduler outranking poll when mux set is active?
Consider adding a comment explaining why scheduler mode outranks poll mode when a mux set is active, to help future maintainers understand this design decision.
